module: Define the system and its compliance boundary

lesson.title: Build the scope record: case exercise
lesson.summary: Produce a conditional scope record rather than a broad compliance claim.

prerequisites.reason: Date the duties Preserve parallel checks.

blocks: Case file: Northbridge supplies an inference-based candidate-ranking service to EU employers under its own name. Its specified purpose materially influences recruitment shortlisting. These are stipulated facts, not conclusions about a real supplier.
The employer operates it under its authority. Record Northbridge as provider and employer as deployer; distinguish upstream components and any additional supply-chain actors.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2, 3, 6, 111, 113; Annex III 4(a)

blocks: The supplied purpose matches Annex III 4(a). No Article 6(3) exception is established. Do not substitute “a human decides” for the complete exception analysis.
Write the exact purpose, point, factual basis and unresolved evidence. If the facts change, reopen classification rather than copying the previous conclusion.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2, 3, 6, 111, 113; Annex III 4(a)

blocks: The case uses the amended Annex III Chapter III Sections 1–3 date: 2 December 2027, subject to relevant exceptions and Article 111 evidence. First-supply dates and later design changes are not supplied in this case.
Keep transition status unresolved. Do not fabricate an invoice date or claim the legacy provision definitely applies.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2, 3, 6, 111, 113; Annex III 4(a)

blocks: Suggested dossier entry: “High-risk Annex III recruitment purpose on stated facts; Northbridge provider; employer deployer; Chapter III date identified; legacy facts unresolved.”
Keep Article 5, Article 50, data-law and sector/national questions open for their own tests. This scope record starts the compliance work; it does not establish that every release gate has been met.
